source.title: Completeness of sets of complex exponentials in convex sets: open problems

accepted.question_text: Let Λ = {λ_n} be a sequence of pairwise distinct complex numbers with 0 not in Λ and λ_n tending to infinity. For X = [-a,a] with a > 0 on the real axis, take H(X) = C[-a,a], and let Exp Λ = {exp(λ_n z)}. Completeness means that the closure of the linear span of Exp Λ in H(X) equals H(X). What precise condition, preferably expressed through the density of Λ and the geometry of X, characterizes exactly when Exp Λ is complete in C[-a,a]?

evidence.quote: Let Λ = {λ_n}, n ∈ N, be a sequence of pairwise different complex numbers (points) in the complex plane C, 0 ∉ Λ, and λ_n → ∞ as n → +∞. Let X be a convex open or closed set on C. By H(X) denote the space of all continuous complex-valued functions on X which are holomorpic in the interior Int X of X (if Int X ≠ ∅) with the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets of X. An exponential system Exp Λ = {exp(λ_n z)} is complete in X if the closure of the linear span of Exp Λ in H(X) coincides with H(X).
1) X = [-a,a] is a segment on real axis R, a > 0, and H(X) = C[-a,a].

(1-?) No precise condition is known for the completeness of systems Exp Λ in [-a,a], and finding such a condition is a very difficult problem. In this case we present a test for the completeness of systems Exp Λ in [-a,a] to within a single exponential.

accepted.question_text: Let Λ = {λ_n} be a sequence of pairwise distinct complex numbers with 0 not in Λ and λ_n tending to infinity, and let Exp Λ = {exp(λ_n z)}. For X equal to one of the intervals (-a,a) with 0 < a ≤ +∞, [0,+∞), or (-∞,0], with H(X) the space of continuous complex-valued functions on X that are holomorphic in the interior and carry the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets, which sequences Λ make Exp Λ complete in H(X)?

evidence.quote: Let Λ = {λ_n}, n ∈ N, be a sequence of pairwise different complex numbers (points) in the complex plane C, 0 ∉ Λ, and λ_n → ∞ as n → +∞. Let X be a convex open or closed set on C. By H(X) denote the space of all continuous complex-valued functions on X which are holomorpic in the interior Int X of X (if Int X ≠ ∅) with the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets of X. An exponential system Exp Λ = {exp(λ_n z)} is complete in X if the closure of the linear span of Exp Λ in H(X) coincides with H(X).
(2-!) In this case the completeness problem was solved completely by the profound Beurling-Malliavin theorem on the radius of completeness [1].

accepted.question_text: Let Λ = {λ_n} be a sequence of pairwise distinct complex numbers with 0 not in Λ and λ_n tending to infinity, and let Exp Λ = {exp(λ_n z)}. Let G be an unbounded convex domain in the complex plane that contains [0,+∞). With H(G) the space of continuous complex-valued functions on G that are holomorphic in the interior and carry the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets, which sequences Λ make Exp Λ complete in H(G)?

evidence.quote: Let Λ = {λ_n}, n ∈ N, be a sequence of pairwise different complex numbers (points) in the complex plane C, 0 ∉ Λ, and λ_n → ∞ as n → +∞. Let X be a convex open or closed set on C. By H(X) denote the space of all continuous complex-valued functions on X which are holomorpic in the interior Int X of X (if Int X ≠ ∅) with the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets of X. An exponential system Exp Λ = {exp(λ_n z)} is complete in X if the closure of the linear span of Exp Λ in H(X) coincides with H(X).
3) X = G is an unbounded convex domain in C, [0,+∞) ⊂ G.
(3-!) When X = G is an unbounded convex domain in C, the completeness problem was solved completely in [3, Theorem 2].

accepted.question_text: Let Λ = {λ_n} be a sequence of pairwise distinct complex numbers with 0 not in Λ and λ_n tending to infinity, and let Exp Λ = {exp(λ_n z)}. Let G be an unbounded convex domain in the complex plane containing [0,+∞), let Clos G be its closure, and define the width d_G by d_G = lim_{x→+∞} d_G(x), where d_G(x) is the supremum of |z−z′| over z,z′ ∈ G with Re z = Re z′ = x. For the remaining finite-width situations in which the available test for completeness of Exp Λ in H(Clos G) applies only when Λ is separated from the imaginary axis, what precise condition characterizes exactly when Exp Λ is complete in H(Clos G) without imposing that separation hypothesis?

evidence.quote: Let Λ = {λ_n}, n ∈ N, be a sequence of pairwise different complex numbers (points) in the complex plane C, 0 ∉ Λ, and λ_n → ∞ as n → +∞. Let X be a convex open or closed set on C. By H(X) denote the space of all continuous complex-valued functions on X which are holomorpic in the interior Int X of X (if Int X ≠ ∅) with the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets of X. An exponential system Exp Λ = {exp(λ_n z)} is complete in X if the closure of the linear span of Exp Λ in H(X) coincides with H(X).
4) X = Clos G, where G is the same as above, Clos G is the closure of G.
(4-?) The width of an unbounded convex domain G, [0,+∞) ⊂ G, is defined to be the quantity d_G = lim_{x→+∞} d_G(x), where d_G(x) = sup{|z−z′| : z,z′ ∈ G; Re z = Re z′ = x}, x ∈ [0,+∞).
In the opposite case, there is a test for the completeness of a system Exp Λ in Clos G only under conditions that the sequence Λ is separated from the imaginary axis.

accepted.question_text: Let Λ = {λ_n} be a sequence of pairwise distinct complex numbers with 0 not in Λ and λ_n tending to infinity, and let Exp Λ = {exp(λ_n z)}. Let G be a bounded convex domain in the complex plane, and let H(G) be the space of continuous complex-valued functions on G that are holomorphic in the interior and carry the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets. What satisfactory precise criterion, preferably more transparent than a criterion using the full class of Green-function or Jensen-function test functions, characterizes exactly when Exp Λ is complete in H(G)?

evidence.quote: Let Λ = {λ_n}, n ∈ N, be a sequence of pairwise different complex numbers (points) in the complex plane C, 0 ∉ Λ, and λ_n → ∞ as n → +∞. Let X be a convex open or closed set on C. By H(X) denote the space of all continuous complex-valued functions on X which are holomorpic in the interior Int X of X (if Int X ≠ ∅) with the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets of X. An exponential system Exp Λ = {exp(λ_n z)} is complete in X if the closure of the linear span of Exp Λ in H(X) coincides with H(X).
5) X = G is a bounded convex domain in C.

(5-?) At present the completeness problem has not been solved satisfactorily for any bounded convex domain G. In our article [5, Theorem 5] we give a complete solution of the completeness problem in a bounded convex domain G in terms of so-called Jensen functions.
In this theorem, the class G of Green functions plays the role of test functions. However, the class G is too wide. Some more transparent sufficient conditions can be extracted from the Theorem 3.

accepted.question_text: Let Λ = {λ_n} be a sequence of pairwise distinct complex numbers with 0 not in Λ and λ_n tending to infinity, and let Exp Λ = {exp(λ_n z)}. Let K be a compact convex set in the complex plane with nonempty interior, and let H(K) be the space of continuous complex-valued functions on K that are holomorphic in the interior and carry the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets. What precise condition characterizes exactly when Exp Λ is complete in H(K)?

evidence.quote: Let Λ = {λ_n}, n ∈ N, be a sequence of pairwise different complex numbers (points) in the complex plane C, 0 ∉ Λ, and λ_n → ∞ as n → +∞. Let X be a convex open or closed set on C. By H(X) denote the space of all continuous complex-valued functions on X which are holomorpic in the interior Int X of X (if Int X ≠ ∅) with the topology of uniform convergence on compact subsets of X. An exponential system Exp Λ = {exp(λ_n z)} is complete in X if the closure of the linear span of Exp Λ in H(X) coincides with H(X).
6) X = K, where K is a compact convex set in C, Int K ≠ ∅.

(6-?) No precise condition is known for the completeness of systems Exp Λ in K. The completeness problem in K is apparently a very difficult problem (cf. with X = [-a,a]). We present a test for the completeness of systems Exp Λ in K to within two exponentials.
